publisher: United Nations Statistics Division, UN Comtrade Database (data as reported to the UN by India: Directorate General of Commercial Intelligence and Statistics, Ministry of Commerce and Industry)
title: UN Comtrade: India (reporter 699), annual merchandise trade, all commodities (HS TOTAL), exports and imports by partner
licence: UN Comtrade terms of use (https://comtradeplus.un.org/); free public preview API, cite as 'United Nations Comtrade Database'. No explicit open licence was checked during this task.
method: Fetched with scripts/data/fetch_trade.py from the keyless public preview API, one call per calendar year 1988-2026 (the preview allows only one period per call, max 500 records), all nine partners and both flows per call. Kept records with partner2Code 0, customsCode C00, motCode 0, cmdCode TOTAL. exports_usd = flow X primaryValue, imports_usd = flow M primaryValue, copied as returned (US$, decimals kept). The HS vintage of each year (H0-H6) is recorded in the note column. Five partner-years (CN 2024, BD 2010, PK 2019, NP 1995, AF 2021) were re-queried separately and matched exactly.
coverage: India with China, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Nepal, Bhutan, Sri Lanka, Myanmar, Maldives and Afghanistan; calendar years 1988-2025; 340 partner-years with both exports and imports. Bhutan 1988-1989 has no India-reported record (blank rows). 2026 not yet available as of 2026-10-16.
limitations: Reporter versus partner (mirror) data: these are India's own declarations. The partner's figures for the same trade differ, because imports are valued CIF and exports FOB, because of timing, classification and country-of-origin versus consignment rules, and because of unrecorded or informal border trade (large for Nepal, Bangladesh, Myanmar and Afghanistan). Example: for 2023 China reported imports from India of US$18.54 bn and exports to India of US$117.68 bn, against India's figures of US$16.25 bn exports to and US$121.97 bn imports from China. Exports include re-exports and imports include goods re-imported; goods shipped through third countries (for example India-Pakistan trade via the UAE or Singapore) are counted against the intermediate country, not the neighbour, so trade with Pakistan and Afghanistan in particular is understated. Values are nominal current US$ converted by India at its own exchange rates; they are not adjusted for inflation or rupee movements. Calendar years, not India's April-March fiscal year, so they do not match Ministry of Commerce annual totals. HS revisions (H0 to H6) change detail but not the TOTAL concept. Recent years, especially 2025, may be revised. Comtrade flags these annual totals as aggregates (isAggregate true, isReported false), i.e. summed by UNSD from India's detailed submission. Cross-check against the Ministry of Commerce Export Import Data Bank (tradestat.commerce.gov.in, country-wise total trade, US$ million, fiscal years) is broadly consistent for imports; on 2026-10-16 the EIDB page showed 2023-24 export figures roughly double the adjacent years for all nine partners (e.g. China 33,317.82 vs 15,306.10 in 2022-23 and 14,252.21 in 2024-25), which looks like an error on that page.
